changed.description: Whether the file changed. `false` for a dry run and for a change that changes nothing.

dry_run.description: A dry run: what `reset` would remove; nothing was written.

file_removed.description: The settings file no longer exists after the change (nothing was left in it).

keys.description: The keys whose value changed (for `reset`, the keys it removes), in the order of [`OPTIONS`].

restore_point.description: The restore point after the change: the `.previous` copy, or `null` when there is none.

ChangeAction.description: The verbs that change the settings.

oneOf.description: One option set.
One key removed.
Restore defaults.
Back to the restore point.

Kind.description: What kind of value an option holds.

oneOf.description: On or off.
A whole number.
A number that may have a fraction.
A texture edge in pixels: a power of two.
A list of names or patterns.
A list of record ids, eight hex digits each.
A table of record id (eight hex digits) to a number, written `id=number`.

OptionState.description: One option with the value a Profile gives it.

default.description: The value it takes when the file does not set it; `null` when the generator decides.

kind.description: What kind of value it holds.

max.description: The largest value it takes, for numbers.

min.description: The smallest value it takes, for numbers.

overridden.description: The file sets it, even to its default value.

value.description: The value it takes: the file's when the file sets it, else the default.

Refusal.description:
Why a reading or a change of the settings was refused. `what` is a catalogue string and `detail` is
[`catalogue::NOTHING_CHANGED`]; `key` and `reason` are data beside them.

code.description: The stable code callers match on.

detail.description: What was not changed, from the catalogue.

key.description: The option or file key it is about, when there is one.

reason.description: A further reason for people (a parser's or the generator's own words), never matched on.

what.description: What went wrong, from the catalogue.

oneOf.description: The Instance cannot be opened (exit code 2).
The Profile does not exist (exit code 2).
The file cannot be read or is not TOML (exit code 2).
A key that is not an option (exit code 2).
A value of the wrong kind (exit code 2).
A value outside its option's range (exit code 2).
A texture size that is not a power of two (exit code 2).
A record id that is not eight hex digits (exit code 2).
An empty name in a list (exit code 2).
The generator's own check refused the settings (exit code 2).
Undo without a restore point (exit code 2).
The file could not be written (exit code 4).

Warning.description: Something the settings allow but that quietly builds less than asked: a warning, never a refusal.

code.description: The stable code callers match on.

reason.description: A further reason for people, never matched on.

value.description: The value it is about (a world or plugin name), when there is one.

what.description: What it means, from the catalogue.

oneOf.description: A world in `worlds` that no active plugin defines.
The plugins could not be read to check `worlds`.
A plugin in an inclusion rule that is not active in the Profile.
Every plugin in `only_plugins` is also in `exclude_plugins`: no object is left.

description: The document `raul lod settings ... --json` prints (Contract `raul-lod-settings`, version 1).

change.description: What the command changed; `null` for `show` and for a refusal.

error.description: Set when the command was refused; nothing changed then.

file.description: The settings file, or `null` when the Profile could not be resolved.

options.description:
Every option with its value after the command (unchanged after a refusal); empty when the settings cannot be
read.

profile.description: The Profile, or empty when it could not be resolved.

restore_point.description: The restore point Undo goes back to, or `null`.

run_in_progress.description: A LOD run of the Profile is going: it uses the settings it started with, and a change applies to the next run.

warnings.description:
What the settings allow but would quietly build nothing or fail on: unknown worlds, inactive plugins in the
inclusion rules, rules that leave no object. Never a refusal.
